pathway.title: TENET HEALTHCARE CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings momentum is the main support. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026 and the issuer raised its FY2026 outlook to USD 5,050 million to USD 5,200 million, but the quarter includes a net favorable USD 147 million of timing items from the CommonSpirit transition; on an analyst adjustment that removes it, leverage would be 2.18x rather than 2.11x, still moderate, so the credit does not depend on that benefit. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation CALC-F8; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable. Cash of USD 2,674 million and undrawn revolver availability of USD 1,900 million total USD 4,574 million against debt due within a year of USD 164 million, notes of USD 1,850 million due in 2028, USD 1,400 million due in 2029 and USD 3,450 million due in 2030, so a market closure would not force a near-term default. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation CALC-F7; calculation CALC-F9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth, not cash retention. Underlying last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 2,788 million, after excluding the USD 540 million CommonSpirit set-off, is outweighed by distributions of USD 838 million to minority partners, repurchases of USD 1,813 million and acquisitions of USD 243 million, which total USD 2,894 million, so net debt rose to USD 10,569 million from USD 10,288 million while leverage fell. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-F1; calculation CALC-F2; calculation CALC-F3; calculation CALC-F4; calculation CALC-F5; calculation CALC-F6

Policy risk is concentrated from 2027 and is the primary downside. The 2025 federal budget law can cap state-directed Medicaid payments and limit provider taxes from 2027, expired exchange subsidies are already lowering exchange admissions, and government programs and managed care together supply most hospital revenue, so a payment cut would hit Hospital margin first. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings quality and minority leakage mean consolidated leverage understates pressure on creditors. Reported EBITDA includes USD 1,472 million of contract termination revenue in nine months 2026 that the issuer excludes from adjusted measures, and 39.35% of Ambulatory Adjusted EBITDA belongs to minority partners, so cash available to Tenet's creditors is lower than the consolidated ratio implies. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3

Financial policy is shareholder-oriented but funded from cash flow. With no sponsor, repurchases of USD 1,615 million in nine months 2026, USD 1,875 million of remaining authorization and no limit on distributions in the secured note indentures leave policy to management, and the record so far shows secured debt cut rather than increased. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148

Refinancing has reduced secured debt but raised the share of unsecured claims. Secured notes fell from USD 9,800 million to USD 8,300 million while unsecured notes rose from USD 2,862 million to USD 4,362 million, which helps secured holders and the 2027 maturity wall but puts more claims at the unsecured rank that sits behind the revolver and secured notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation CALC-F10

The CommonSpirit note is a modest net positive with concentrated counterparty risk. Payments of about USD 453 million a year from January 2027 would offset part of the leakage to partners if applied to debt, but they depend on one counterparty and replace a contract that ran to 2032. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Strengths: scale and diversification across a hospital network in eight states and a surgery-center platform in 37 states; improving margins in both segments; adjusted net leverage of 2.11x; ample liquidity with an undrawn revolver; fixed-rate notes with no maturity before 2028; and a reduction in secured debt in September 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3

Weaknesses: reliance on reimbursement set by government programs and a few large managed care payers; consolidated earnings that include large minority interests; reported earnings inflated by contract termination revenue; a shareholder-return policy that leaves almost no retained cash flow; a combined chairman and chief executive role; and exposure to one counterparty for the CommonSpirit receivable. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Three transactions shaped the capital structure since the last fiscal year end. On 2026-01-27 Tenet agreed with CommonSpirit Health to end the Conifer revenue cycle contract, redeem CommonSpirit's minority interest in Conifer for USD 540 million with effect from 2026-01-01, and receive USD 1,900 million of consideration, of which USD 540 million was set off and USD 1,360 million is a non-interest-bearing note payable in three annual installments of about USD 453 million, the first due in January 2027. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

In November 2025 Tenet issued USD 1,500 million of first lien notes due 2032 and USD 750 million of unsecured notes due 2033, redeemed USD 1,500 million of second lien notes due 2027 and USD 750 million of its unsecured notes due 2028, and replaced its revolving credit facility with a USD 1,900 million asset-based facility maturing on 2030-11-04. In September 2026 it issued USD 2,000 million of unsecured notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all USD 1,500 million of the first lien notes due 2027 and USD 500 million of the unsecured notes due 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 2

The sources read describe no acquisition financing beyond internal cash: nine-month 2026 acquisition spending was USD 201 million against USD 266 million a year earlier, and no new sponsor, merger or leveraged transaction is disclosed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

fields.value: Business and governance review of TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (issuer thc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, shareholder and capital-allocation behavior and issuer history, from the annual report, the latest quarterly report and the latest earnings release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tenet is publicly held with no sponsor in the documents read, so creditor risk rests on its own financial policy, which has turned toward large share repurchases that the secured note indentures do not restrict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hospital Operations produced 75.73% of FY2025 net operating revenues, but Ambulatory Care produced 44.37% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, and 39.35% of Ambulatory Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 belongs to minority partners. Repurchases of USD 1,615 million and distributions to minority partners of USD 614 million took 63.56% of nine-month operating cash flow.

fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, so creditor alignment depends on board policy rather than on a sponsor's exit horizon. The common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and held by a broad base of record holders, and the beneficial-ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two segments carry different credit characteristics. Ambulatory Care earned an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 39.17% in FY2025 against 15.74% in Hospital Operations, but its profit is shared with physician and health-system partners, and a hospital network concentrated in a few states carries the reimbursement exposure.

fields.value: Reimbursement policy is the main external credit driver. Managed care payers supplied 45.50% of FY2025 net operating revenues and Medicare and Medicaid together 17.10%, and the issuer warns that the 2025 federal budget law could cut Medicaid supplemental payments from 2027 and that expired exchange subsidies may raise the uninsured share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have grown faster than debt reduction. Repurchases rose from USD 672 million in FY2024 to USD 1,386 million in FY2025 and USD 1,615 million in nine months 2026, and the board added USD 2,000 million of authorization in June 2026, leaving USD 1,875 million available at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capacity for distributions is wide but behavior has so far been funded from operating cash flow and refinancing. The secured note indentures state no restriction on additional debt, restricted payments, dividends or repurchases, yet in nine months 2026 borrowings of USD 2,041 million were slightly below repayments of USD 2,087 million while operating cash flow was USD 3,507 million, so repurchases did not rely on new net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing has cut secured debt and pushed maturities out. The September 2026 transaction cut secured notes from USD 9,800 million to USD 8,300 million by moving the 2027 secured maturity into unsecured notes due 2034, which lengthens maturities but leaves more debt at the unsecured rank, and the revolver stayed undrawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The CommonSpirit agreement converted a long contract into a receivable and a full ownership interest. Tenet regained 100% of Conifer from 23.8% minority ownership and ended a revenue cycle contract that had run to 2032, in return for a note of USD 1,360 million repayable in three annual installments of about USD 453 million from January 2027, which adds near-term cash but removes contracted revenue and creates exposure to CommonSpirit's payment performance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance disclosure supports monitoring but not control analysis. The audited statements carry unqualified opinions and adjusted measures are reconciled to GAAP, but the proxy statement, board composition, large-holder ownership and executive pay were not supplied, and one executive holds both the chairman and chief executive roles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is that large repurchases coincided with lower leverage: the issuer reports net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 2.11x at 2026-09-30 against 2.25x at 2025-12-31, the revolver has no borrowings and secured notes fell by USD 1,500 million in September 2026. The view would turn more cautious if repurchases were funded by revolver draws or new debt, if leverage rose while the CommonSpirit note was still outstanding, or if state Medicaid supplemental payments were cut from 2027 without offsetting costs; it would turn more favorable if the board held repurchases within free cash flow and applied part of the CommonSpirit receipts to debt.

fields.value: Three transactions shaped the capital structure since the last fiscal year end. On 2026-01-27 Tenet agreed with CommonSpirit Health to end the Conifer revenue cycle contract, redeem CommonSpirit's minority interest in Conifer for USD 540 million with effect from 2026-01-01, and receive USD 1,900 million of consideration, of which USD 540 million was set off and USD 1,360 million is a non-interest-bearing note payable in three annual installments of about USD 453 million, the first due in January 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In November 2025 Tenet issued USD 1,500 million of first lien notes due 2032 and USD 750 million of unsecured notes due 2033, redeemed USD 1,500 million of second lien notes due 2027 and USD 750 million of its unsecured notes due 2028, and replaced its revolving credit facility with a USD 1,900 million asset-based facility maturing on 2030-11-04. In September 2026 it issued USD 2,000 million of unsecured notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all USD 1,500 million of the first lien notes due 2027 and USD 500 million of the unsecured notes due 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (issuer thc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's overall credit profile, strengths and weaknesses, downside pathway and monitoring triggers, built on the financial foundation, business and governance review and source documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tenet's fundamental credit profile is strong and improving on earnings and liquidity, but creditors rely on EBITDA growth for deleveraging because shareholder returns, minority distributions and acquisitions absorb all underlying free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 2.11x at 2026-09-30 against 2.25x at 2025-12-31, liquidity of USD 4,574 million covers the nearest notes maturity of USD 1,850 million in 2028 by 2.47x, and the main downside is policy-driven Hospital earnings pressure from 2027 on debt that is fixed in rate and size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation CALC-F7; calculation CALC-F9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings momentum is the main support. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026 and the issuer raised its FY2026 outlook to USD 5,050 million to USD 5,200 million, but the quarter includes a net favorable USD 147 million of timing items from the CommonSpirit transition; on an analyst adjustment that removes it, leverage would be 2.18x rather than 2.11x, still moderate, so the credit does not depend on that benefit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation CALC-F8; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are comfortable. Cash of USD 2,674 million and undrawn revolver availability of USD 1,900 million total USD 4,574 million against debt due within a year of USD 164 million, notes of USD 1,850 million due in 2028, USD 1,400 million due in 2029 and USD 3,450 million due in 2030, so a market closure would not force a near-term default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation CALC-F7; calculation CALC-F9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth, not cash retention. Underlying last-twelve-month free cash flow of USD 2,788 million, after excluding the USD 540 million CommonSpirit set-off, is outweighed by distributions of USD 838 million to minority partners, repurchases of USD 1,813 million and acquisitions of USD 243 million, which total USD 2,894 million, so net debt rose to USD 10,569 million from USD 10,288 million while leverage fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-F1; calculation CALC-F2; calculation CALC-F3; calculation CALC-F4; calculation CALC-F5; calculation CALC-F6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy risk is concentrated from 2027 and is the primary downside. The 2025 federal budget law can cap state-directed Medicaid payments and limit provider taxes from 2027, expired exchange subsidies are already lowering exchange admissions, and government programs and managed care together supply most hospital revenue, so a payment cut would hit Hospital margin first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality and minority leakage mean consolidated leverage understates pressure on creditors. Reported EBITDA includes USD 1,472 million of contract termination revenue in nine months 2026 that the issuer excludes from adjusted measures, and 39.35% of Ambulatory Adjusted EBITDA belongs to minority partners, so cash available to Tenet's creditors is lower than the consolidated ratio implies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is shareholder-oriented but funded from cash flow. With no sponsor, repurchases of USD 1,615 million in nine months 2026, USD 1,875 million of remaining authorization and no limit on distributions in the secured note indentures leave policy to management, and the record so far shows secured debt cut rather than increased.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 148

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing has reduced secured debt but raised the share of unsecured claims. Secured notes fell from USD 9,800 million to USD 8,300 million while unsecured notes rose from USD 2,862 million to USD 4,362 million, which helps secured holders and the 2027 maturity wall but puts more claims at the unsecured rank that sits behind the revolver and secured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The CommonSpirit note is a modest net positive with concentrated counterparty risk. Payments of about USD 453 million a year from January 2027 would offset part of the leakage to partners if applied to debt, but they depend on one counterparty and replace a contract that ran to 2032.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a favorable view is that retained cash flow is already negative on an underlying basis (a shortfall of USD 106 million over the last twelve months) while policy risk starts in 2027, so a Hospital earnings setback would leave leverage to rise one for one with debt fixed. The view would turn more cautious if guidance were cut, if net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose above the 2.25x of 2025-12-31, or if repurchases were funded from the revolver or new debt; it would turn more favorable if the board held shareholder returns within free cash flow and applied the CommonSpirit receipts to debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: scale and diversification across a hospital network in eight states and a surgery-center platform in 37 states; improving margins in both segments; adjusted net leverage of 2.11x; ample liquidity with an undrawn revolver; fixed-rate notes with no maturity before 2028; and a reduction in secured debt in September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses: reliance on reimbursement set by government programs and a few large managed care payers; consolidated earnings that include large minority interests; reported earnings inflated by contract termination revenue; a shareholder-return policy that leaves almost no retained cash flow; a combined chairman and chief executive role; and exposure to one counterparty for the CommonSpirit receivable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_thc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tenet is a publicly held operator of 50 hospitals and a surgery-center platform, so there is no sponsor whose exit or extraction behavior could harm creditors, and the issue for creditors is board policy. Hospital Operations provides about three quarters of revenue and a lower margin, while Ambulatory Care provides a quarter of revenue and a larger share of Adjusted EBITDA but shares profit with physician and health-system partners, which makes consolidated EBITDA an upper bound on cash reaching Tenet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring and non-discretionary in nature, but price is set by third parties: managed care contracts renewed on negotiated rates, and Medicare and Medicaid rates set by government. Pricing power is therefore moderate, volume growth is supported by acuity and admissions, and the exposure to supplemental Medicaid payments and exchange coverage creates policy-driven revenue risk rather than cyclical demand risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161; 10-K_2025-12-31_thc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_thc-20260930ex991earningsr.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labor is the largest cost and is exposed to nurse shortages, California staffing ratios and wage inflation, so margin depends on productivity and mix. The Hospital margin recovered to 19.2% in the third quarter from 15.1% a year earlier despite payer mix headwinds, but the quarter includes timing benefits, so margin resilience under a payment cut is not yet tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and flexible, with capital expenditure of USD 910 million over the last twelve months, and conversion of adjusted EBITDA into reported free cash flow of 66.51% falls once the CommonSpirit set-off and distributions to partners are removed. Cash interest paid of USD 830 million is covered 6.03 times by adjusted EBITDA, so debt service is not the constraint; capital allocation is.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-F1; calculation CALC-F2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power sits with managed care payers and government programs, which set price. Competition comes from not-for-profit systems with tax advantages, physician-owned specialty hospitals and outpatient centers, and insurers and private equity buyers of providers, while certificate-of-need rules in some states limit new entry. The shift of surgery to outpatient settings favors the surgery-center platform. Policy is the dominant external factor, labor scarcity is the dominant input factor, and cyber risk is real given the 2022 incident.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tailwinds are rising acuity and admissions, the outpatient shift, cost discipline and the removal of near-term secured maturities; headwinds are the 2027 Medicaid provisions, expired exchange subsidies, payer mix, labor costs and the loss of the contracted CommonSpirit revenue stream after 2026. Management expects a higher outlook for FY2026, which supports near-term credit metrics.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a cap on state-directed Medicaid payments or a deeper loss of exchange coverage from 2027. The first operational break would be lower supplemental revenue and a worse payer mix in Hospital Operations, already visible in lower exchange admissions. The financial transmission is lower Hospital Adjusted EBITDA on a largely fixed cost base, with consolidated leverage rising one for one because debt is fixed in rate and size. Liquidity would hold, since cash and the revolver exceed the nearest maturities, so the consequence is higher leverage and a slower return to shareholders rather than a liquidity crisis. Observable triggers are a guidance cut, falling Hospital margin, state approvals of directed payments and a pause in repurchases.
